name: Hot-air balloon
kidDefinition: A big balloon that lifts a basket into the sky using warm air.
dateBasis: The Montgolfier brothers demonstrate balloon flight at Versailles.
ambiguityNotes: This is a full-size flight milestone, not the origin of small sky lanterns.
funFact: A sheep, a duck, and a rooster rode in a balloon before people did!

name: Electric battery
kidDefinition: A device that stores energy to power electrical things.
dateBasis: Volta introduces his electric battery, called the voltaic pile.
ambiguityNotes: This date refers to the voltaic pile, not modern rechargeable batteries.
funFact: The first electric battery was called a “pile.”

name: Steam locomotive
kidDefinition: An engine that uses steam to pull train carriages along rails.
dateBasis: Trevithick builds early steam railway locomotives.
ambiguityNotes: Museum accounts differ between an 1803 engine and the successful 1804 railway journey; use a range and avoid close comparisons.
funFact: One of Trevithick’s locomotives was named “Catch Me Who Can.”

name: Telephone
kidDefinition: A device for talking with someone who is far away.
dateBasis: Bell receives his telephone patent and demonstrates working speech transmission.
ambiguityNotes: Several inventors contributed; this date marks Bell’s successful patent and demonstration.
funFact: Bell’s famous early telephone message asked his assistant to come to him.

name: Phonograph
kidDefinition: A machine that records sound and plays it back.
dateBasis: Edison develops a phonograph that records and plays back sound.
ambiguityNotes: Earlier devices recorded sound without playing it back.
funFact: Recording sound and playing it back were once two different challenges!

name: Edison’s light bulb
kidDefinition: A glass bulb with a thin wire inside that glows when electricity flows.
dateBasis: Edison’s team makes an incandescent bulb that shines for over 13 hours.
ambiguityNotes: Earlier electric lights existed. This is Edison’s improved bulb, not the first electric light.
funFact: Edison’s team tried hundreds of experiments while working on their light bulb.

name: Gasoline car
kidDefinition: A vehicle whose engine uses gasoline to carry people along roads.
dateBasis: Benz develops his practical gasoline car and files its patent.
ambiguityNotes: Steam vehicles predate gasoline cars; this comparison specifically means Benz’s gasoline automobile.
funFact: Benz’s first gasoline car had three wheels!

name: Cochran’s dishwasher
kidDefinition: A modern practical dishwasher: a machine that washes plates, cups, and other dishes.
dateBasis: Cochran receives a patent for her practical dishwashing machine.
ambiguityNotes: Earlier dishwashing-machine attempts existed; this is the practical Cochran design.
funFact: Cochran designed separate wire spaces to hold plates, cups, and saucers.

name: Modern air conditioner
kidDefinition: A machine that cools the air inside a room or building.
dateBasis: Carrier’s modern system controls temperature and humidity in a printing plant.
ambiguityNotes: Earlier cooling methods existed; this means modern controlled air conditioning.
funFact: Carrier’s first air-conditioning installation helped a printing factory.

name: Powered airplane
kidDefinition: A flying machine with wings and an engine.
dateBasis: The Wright brothers make controlled, powered flights at Kitty Hawk.
ambiguityNotes: Gliders and balloons came earlier. This date means controlled, powered heavier-than-air flight.
funFact: The Wright brothers made four flights on their big day.

name: Slinky
kidDefinition: A spring toy that can stretch, wobble, and step down stairs.
dateBasis: Richard James discovers the spring motion that leads to the Slinky toy.
ambiguityNotes: This is the invention’s origin; the toy was first sold in 1945.
funFact: The Slinky began with springs meant to keep equipment steady on ships.

name: Microwave oven
kidDefinition: A kitchen appliance that uses microwaves to heat food.
dateBasis: Percy Spencer creates a device that cooks food with microwaves.
ambiguityNotes: This is an experimental cooking device, not the later home appliance launch.
funFact: The first microwave oven was given the name “Radarange.”

name: Velcro fastener
kidDefinition: Two strips that stick together using tiny hooks and loops.
dateBasis: From de Mestral’s burr-inspired idea to his US hook-and-loop patent.
ambiguityNotes: Development spanned years. We use the broad idea-to-patent range and exclude overlapping comparisons.
funFact: Clingy plant burrs inspired the tiny hooks in Velcro.

name: Space satellite
kidDefinition: A human-made object sent into space to travel around a planet.
dateBasis: Sputnik becomes the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth.
ambiguityNotes: This means an artificial Earth satellite, not a natural moon.
funFact: The first space satellite was about the size of a beach ball.

name: Stud-and-tube LEGO brick
kidDefinition: A toy building brick with bumps and tubes that help it click together.
dateBasis: LEGO files the patent for its stud-and-tube brick connection.
ambiguityNotes: Earlier LEGO bricks existed; this specifically means the familiar stud-and-tube design.
funFact: The tubes underneath a LEGO brick help it grip other bricks.

name: Computer mouse
kidDefinition: A handheld tool that moves the pointer on a computer screen.
dateBasis: Engelbart’s team develops its first computer mouse prototype.
ambiguityNotes: Prototype milestone; its famous public demonstration was in 1968.
funFact: The first computer mouse had a wooden shell and just one button.

name: Rubik’s Cube
kidDefinition: A twisty puzzle with colored squares you try to match on each side.
dateBasis: Ernő Rubik creates his twisting cube puzzle.
ambiguityNotes: Invention date, not the 1980 international release.
funFact: The Rubik’s Cube was first called the “Magic Cube.”

name: Digital camera
kidDefinition: A camera that saves pictures as electronic information.
dateBasis: Steven Sasson builds a self-contained digital camera at Kodak.
ambiguityNotes: This means a self-contained digital camera, not earlier photographic or electronic imaging systems.
